$comment: Mission 1.74.1. The operator approved dispatch of ONE enquiry. This record sits BESIDE the frozen packet rather than inside it, because Mission 1.66 settled that marking a frozen document APPROVED changes the bytes that were approved -- and here it would not even move the packet's digest, since that covers only the six binding fields, and it would still change the artifact the operator read.

approval.$comment: The approval names a document by its hash, recomputed rather than asserted.
approval.why: Mission 1.66. An approval flag written into the frozen packet would change the artifact the operator read, and the packet's own validator asserts that the packet records no approval. That field means THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO APPROVAL and never that no approval exists.

approved_action.$comment: Mission 1.65's envelope rule, one layer out: the digest binds the ACTION and excludes itself, the execution status and the recorded date. Changing the mechanism, the target, the identity or the title produces a different approval that SUPERSEDES this one rather than editing it.
approved_action.approved_title: HTTP measurement: is a 3xx response returned without following the redirect?
approved_action.channel_match_basis: the packet's channel is PUBLIC_TECHNICAL_CHANNEL and its recipient is the provider's public issue tracker; the approved mechanism posts one public issue on that tracker, so the approved action is the action the packet describes
approved_action.why_that_differs_from_mission_1_66: the ONYPHE envelope bound a PLACEHOLDER sender, because under manual email the sender is not determined until the send, and Mission 1.65 stated that cost in advance: the hash pinned three fields of four. Here the destination is a public repository rather than a mailbox, so mechanism, target, identity and title are all determined before the act. The cost stated there does not recur here.

execution.$comment: An approval says an action MAY be performed. Only a performance says it WAS, and this record must not fill itself in -- every field an execution needs is already known from the approval, which is exactly what makes a fictional record easy.
execution.why_the_counter_was_split: Mission 1.74.7. The single counter refused every GitHub API call, and Mission 1.74.1 defined the upgrade to BYTE_VERIFIED as a RAW READ of the issue body. Those cannot both hold, so the first legitimate upgrade surfaced the contradiction. What the rule protects is that this repository never WROTE: no issue created, no public post, no gh issue create -- and a read is not that. The write half keeps the refusal at zero. The read half is not merely permitted, it is now REQUIRED to be at least one whenever raw_body_compared is true, because a comparison with no read is a comparison against nothing.
execution.value_preserved_by_the_split: the old counter read 0 and the write counter reads 0. Nothing this repository was forbidden to do became permitted; a distinction the old name could not express was drawn.
execution.why_byte_verification_is_possible_here: Mission 1.66 could reach only OPERATOR_ATTESTED because a manual email send happens inside a mail client nothing here can observe. A public GitHub issue has a durable public URL, so once the operator supplies it the posted title and body can be compared against the approved ones. The ceiling that arc hit is a property of the CHANNEL rather than of manual sending.
execution.upgrade_path: taken. BYTE_VERIFIED is the top of this channel's ladder and there is nothing above it.
execution.reachable_only_through: an explicit operator attestation that the post was made, plus the issue URL. This repository cannot reach SENT by any other route.
execution.why_the_supplied_number_was_not_used: the operator's attestation left issue_number as the template placeholder 'XXXX'. A number was not invented: the URL already carries it, so it is derived from the URL and the two are the same fact stated once rather than an independent confirmation.
execution.attestation_statement: The issue was posted manually by me exactly once using the approved title and frozen body.

corroboration.$comment: Mission 1.63. A RETRIEVAL SUMMARY IS NOT A DOCUMENT. The public page was fetched and converted to markdown by a summarising extraction, so what follows corroborates the attestation and does not replace it.
corroboration.what_this_does_not_establish: byte equality of the body. The extraction rendered the body's paragraph break as a space, which is an artifact of HTML to markdown conversion rather than evidence of a difference -- and precisely because it is an artifact, this retrieval cannot distinguish it from one. Whitespace and exact characters were not compared.
corroboration.therefore_the_level_stays_note: Mission 1.74.7. This says what THAT retrieval established, and it is still true of it: a summarising extraction leaves the level at OPERATOR_ATTESTED. The level moved on a different retrieval, recorded in byte_verification below, and this block was not rewritten to take credit for it.

execution.byte_verification_not_reached_because: superseded by the block below. Mission 1.74.3 could not reach it because its only retrieval passed through a summarising extraction; this mission read the issue through the REST API, which returns the stored markdown.

byte_verification.$comment: Mission 1.74.7. The upgrade Mission 1.74.3 specified and did not take, taken on the read that fetching the provider's reply required anyway.
byte_verification.what_the_endpoint_returns: the stored markdown of the issue body, not a rendering of it
byte_verification.comparison: character for character, including whitespace and line endings
byte_verification.paragraph_break_artifact_from_1_74_3_exp: the earlier retrieval rendered the body's paragraph break as a space. The raw read shows the break is present in the stored body, so that was an artifact of the HTML-to-markdown conversion exactly as Mission 1.74.3 suspected -- and could not prove, which is why it refused the upgrade rather than assuming.
byte_verification.what_this_establishes: the issue posted at the attested URL carries the approved title and the frozen body, byte for byte. The operator's attestation is now corroborated by a comparison rather than only by a retrieval that could not distinguish an artifact from a difference.
byte_verification.what_this_does_not_establish: that the operator posted it, rather than that it is posted. Authorship still rests on the attestation plus the public author field, and byte verification grades the CONTENT rather than the act.
byte_verification.mission_accounting_above_counts_mission_: this mission's reads are counted in docs/data/globalping-r1-provider-reply-v1.json, which is where Mission 1.74.7's accounting lives

integrity_checks_frozen_before_any_post.$comment: Frozen now, which is the only time they mean anything. A posted issue cannot be unposted, so a duplicate is REPORTED rather than tidied away.

scope.$comment: The operator approved ONE enquiry. The other is untouched.
scope.why_r2_is_not_covered: the operator approved GP-R1-Q1 only, and an approval of one action is not an approval of another that happens to have been prepared alongside it

recommended_next_action.$comment: It belongs to a person, and it happens outside this repository.
recommended_next_action.action: the operator posts one public issue on jsdelivr/globalping and supplies its URL

forward_pointer.$comment: Appended by Mission 1.74.2. Nothing above this field changed. Its scope block says this approval does not cover R2, which is still true; R2 was approved separately and later, by a different mechanism, in its own record.
forward_pointer.what_this_does_not_change: every field this record established when it was written, including that THIS approval covers GP-R1-Q1 alone
